messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a sudden nvme write-latency spike on eu-west3 and ~20% of GPU attaches failing. Example from gnode-233:
```
[2026-03-20T09:41:02Z] nvme0n1: write latency 12.3s, queue depth=128, device busy
_attach: failed to allocate scratch -> provisioning timeout
```
Can someone grab the janitor/evictor logs?

maria: Looking. I see an evictor crash loop on the same nodes with a segfault in the eviction iterator. Not a normal scrub overlap. Snip from janitor.log:
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
goroutine 27 [running]:
github.com/redwood/ephemeral/evictor.(*Iterator).Next(...)
\t/go/src/ephemeral/evictor/iterator.go:142
main.main()
\t/go/src/ephemeral/cmd/janitor/main.go:54
```
Also SMART counters show thermal spikes right before the crash.

jonathan: That kernel rollout happened this morning in eu-west3, ops-bot posted it. Could be an interaction with the new NVMe driver and our iterator code. ops-bot, can you confirm kernel version?

ops-bot: Deploy-bot: rolled out kernel `6.4.8-rw` to eu-west3 at 2026-03-20T06:30Z for telemetry improvements. No rollbacks yet.

tara: If evictor is segfaulting we should stop janitor runs in the region to avoid exacerbating IO. We can flip the janitor-rate to 0.1 for eu-west3 via feature flag and re-route provisioning. Quick mitigation: route gpu attaches away from eu-west3 until we confirm.

maria: +1. I can throttle janitor in-place: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags/janitor_rate -d '{"eu-west3":0.1}'` and push an emergency k8s rollback for the janitor to a non-crashing image (we built a debug image yesterday).

alex: Routing note: shifting 200 concurrent attaches to us-west1 will add ~12% provisioning latency and ~$0.08/min extra for burst GPUs. We should announce to capacity team.

jonathan: I'll update quota engine to prefer us-west1 and add a temporary soft-cap to eu-west3 at 60% so we don't try to jam more. ETA for that change: 10m.

maria: Also saw NVMe device counters incrementing Write Amplification before segfault — logs show sustained small writes from overlayfs GC. Might be a hotpath in the cleaner triggered by kernel change. Full trace: `janitor --v=4 --trace=overlayfs_gc` shows repeated `fsync` stalls.

tara: Plan: 1) throttle janitor in eu-west3 (maria) 2) update quota/routing (jonathan) 3) throttle provisioning and route to us-west1 (jonathan/alex) 4) schedule kernel rollback in eu-west3 if we reproduce (ops) 5) collect crash dumps and open a regression ticket in infra-repo.

ops-bot: Ops-bot: kernel rollback requires change window. Suggest hotfix: pin nvme driver userspace behaviour by disabling overlayfs GC flag `overlay_gc_async=false` via sysctl as intermediate.

maria: I can try `echo 0 > /sys/module/overlay/parameters/gc_async` on one canary node and repro. If that removes the fsync storm and evictor no longer crashes, we avoid immediate kernel rollback.

alex: Can we do that canary now? Need a green check before moving 200 attaches. Also, add emergency slack status channel `#infra-eu-west3-incident` so support sees degraded region.

jonathan: Done — quota change + routing bump applied. I set eu-west3 soft-cap and updated the router policy to fallback to us-west1.

maria: Poked the canary, turning off overlay GC removed the fsync spikes within 2 minutes. Evictor didn't crash after 8m of watch. Uploading crash dump to the ticket.

tara: Good. Next: rollback janitor image to yesterday's build in eu-west3 and keep overlay gc disabled until kernel rollback or driver patch.

alex: I'm posting a short note to capacity and support with the mitigation and cost impact. Please add timeline estimates to the ticket.

maria: Filed infra/evictor#4723 with logs, crash dumps, and mitigation steps. Assigning to `eng-infra` and `eng-runtime` triage.

jonathan: I'll monitor attaches for the next 2 hours and revert routes when stable.

alex: Thanks everyone. If we need to escalate to hardware vendor for thermal anomalies we'll do that, but current signal points at the kernel-driver-interaction.

tara: thumbs up from me. :thumbsup:
